findings.condition: Two terminated users had their Okta accounts suspended/deactivated more than 24 hours after termination: E1006 (Rossi, Kenji) had first suspend event 77 hours after termination (OK-000037), and E1038 (Lee, Ivy) had first deactivate event 89 hours after termination (OK-000153). Owner confirmed both offboarding tickets were actioned late with no approved exceptions.
findings.criteria: Policy section 4.3: 'When a workforce member's engagement ends, IT Operations must suspend or deactivate their Okta account within 24 clock hours of the termination time recorded in the HR system. Weekends and public holidays are not excluded.'
findings.cause: Offboarding tickets were actioned late without approved exceptions
findings.effect: Terminated users retained access to Okta for up to 89 hours beyond the allowed 24-hour window, creating unauthorized access risk
findings.recommendation: Implement automated monitoring and alerts for termination-to-deprovisioning delays, establish escalation procedures for late tickets, and ensure all exceptions are formally documented and approved before implementation

findings.condition: Three pull requests (PR-1316, PR-1229, PR-1017) were merged to main with only the author serving as approver, violating segregation of duties requirements.
findings.criteria: Policy section 3.1: 'At least one approver other than the author must approve the pull request before it is merged.'
findings.cause: Pull request merge controls did not enforce that an approver different from the author must approve before merge.
findings.effect: Production changes were deployed without independent review, increasing risk of unvalidated code entering production.
findings.recommendation: Configure branch protection rules to require at least one approval from a user other than the PR author before allowing merges to main. Implement automated enforcement to prevent self-approval.

findings.condition: Critical vulnerability VULN-0029 was open for 49 days from 2026-05-13 to 2026-07-01, exceeding the 30-day remediation SLA. No risk acceptance was documented for this vulnerability.
findings.criteria: Policy section 2.2: 'Critical vulnerabilities are remediated within 30 calendar days of being opened.' Section 2.3 allows exceptions only with approved, unexpired risk acceptance tickets.
findings.cause: No risk acceptance ticket was created or linked to VULN-0029 despite the 49-day delay exceeding the 30-day SLA threshold.
findings.effect: Critical vulnerability remained unremediated beyond the acceptable timeframe without documented business justification or compensating controls approval.
findings.recommendation: Implement enforcement to require risk acceptance documentation for any critical vulnerability approaching the 30-day SLA threshold. Review VULN-0029 to determine if compensating controls were in place and obtain retroactive approval if warranted, or document why this represents a control failure.
